title: INT8 profile ingestion pipeline and adversarial regression playbook
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: We have multiple sources of INT8 weight-only quantization profiles (GPTQ, AWQ variants, internal conversion scripts) arriving in different schema versions. Ingested profiles are used to select kernel paths, quant scales, and fallback policies at serving time. Recent downstream regressions (small but customer-visible quality deltas on complex prompts) indicate our profile ingestion + regression protection is incomplete. This ticket implements an ingestion pipeline (validation, normalization, artifact fingerprinting) plus an adversarial regression harness and canary playbook to prevent bad profiles from reaching production.

Goals:
- Build a deterministic profile ingestion service that: validates schema v1/v2, normalizes per-layer scale metadata, and computes a canonical fingerprint for provenance.
- Create an adversarial regression test suite that runs new profiles against: golden prompts, fuzzed prompt matrix, and embedding-similarity checks to detect semantic drift.
- Add automated canary rollout logic: shadow deploy -> small-weighted traffic -> automated rollback on quality or latency regression -> rollout ladder.
- Produce a playbook for SRE/RE to follow on detection (investigation steps, telemetry queries, and rollback commands).

Non-goals: full retraining or model-level changes; this is focused on profile ingestion + validation and regression detection, not runbook for quant algorithm changes.
acceptance_criteria: Profile ingestion service (service+batch job) validates schema v1/v2 and rejects malformed profiles with descriptive errors
Every ingested profile receives a stable fingerprint and metadata stored in profile-registry (s3 path + sha256)
Adversarial regression harness runs in CI against a configurable prompt matrix and flags >2% answer-similarity degradation (embedding cosine or token-level BLEU) compared to baseline
Canary rollout automation: shadow test, 1% -> 5% -> 25% ladder with automatic rollback on quality or p99 latency regression
Playbook published in Confluence with runbook steps, dashboard links, and postmortem checklist
technical_notes:
Ingestion should compute per-layer histograms and store quant scale distributions (float32 arrays as base64 payload metadata). Use canonical tokenization alignment checks to ensure scale/kl statistics correspond to expected vocab IDs. Regression harness will use two signal classes: (1) semantic delta via embedding cosine (use bi-encoder reference) and (2) deterministic golden-answer diffs with fuzzy matching for non-deterministic generation. Thresholds: embedding mean cosine drop >0.015 OR golden-answer pass rate drop >2% triggers failure. Latency guard: if p99 increases >20% at canary QPS, fail rollout. Fallback policy: automatically pin to previous profile and trigger asynchronous deeper eval.

Implementation trade-offs:
- Storing per-layer scale histograms increases registry size but enables offline debugging; acceptable given infrequent profile churn.
- Relying on embedding cosine is more robust to generation stochasticity but adds dependency on the reference embedder; mitigate by pinning embedder version in the pipeline.

Telemetry hooks: emit profile.fingerprint, profile.source, regression.embedding_delta.mean, regression.golden_drop, canary.p99_ratio, and rollback_reason tags to telemetry pipeline.
